samples.text: Write chemical formula of washing soda. How is it obtained from baking soda ? List two uses of washing soda.
samples.answer:
Na2CO3.10H2O
When baking soda is heated sodium carbonate is obtained and recrystallisation of sodium carbonate gives washing soda. /
2 NaHCO3 --heat--> Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2
Na2CO3 +10 H2O --> Na2CO3.10 H2O
Uses:
(i)In glass / soap / paper industry
(ii)In manufacture of borax
(iii)As cleansing agent for domestic purpose
(iv)Removing permanent hardness of water (Any Two)
samples.explanation:
• Washing soda's chemical formula is Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.
• It is obtained by heating baking soda (NaHCO₃) to form sodium carbonate, which is then recrystallised with water to yield washing soda crystals.
• Two common uses: manufacturing glass, soap, and paper; and removing permanent hardness of water as a domestic cleansing agent.

samples.text: Common salt is a very important raw material as many compounds of industrial use can be prepared from it. Explain, giving chemical equations, the method of preparation of washing soda from sodium chloride. List four industrial/domestic uses of washing soda.
samples.answer:
• Concentrated solution of sodium chloride reacts with ammonia and carbon dioxide to obtain sodium hydrogen carbonate and ammonium chloride.
• NaCl + NH3 + CO2 + H2O → NaHCO3 + NH4Cl
• When sodium hydrogen carbonate is heated strongly, sodium carbonate is obtained.
• 2NaHCO3 --Heat--> Na2CO3 + CO2 + H2O
• Sodium carbonate is dissolved in water to obtain washing soda.
• Na2CO3 + 10H2O → Na2CO3·10H2O
Uses:
• In glass, soap and paper industries.
• Manufacture of borax.
• As a cleaning agent for domestic purposes.
• For removing permanent hardness of water.
samples.explanation:
Given: Sodium chloride (NaCl) is the raw material for washing soda.
• Step 1: NaCl + NH3 + CO2 + H2O → NaHCO3 + NH4Cl (Solvay process forms sodium hydrogen carbonate).
• Step 2: 2NaHCO3 --heat--> Na2CO3 + CO2 + H2O (heating gives sodium carbonate).
• Step 3: Na2CO3 + 10H2O → Na2CO3·10H2O (crystallisation gives washing soda).
∴ Uses of washing soda: (1) glass, soap and paper industries; (2) manufacture of borax; (3) as a domestic cleaning agent; (4) for removing permanent hardness of water.

samples.text: The melting and boiling points of carbon compounds are generally low and they are largely non-conductors of electricity. State two conclusions based on these two properties.
samples.answer:
• Low melting and boiling points indicate weak intermolecular forces of attraction between molecules.
• Being non-conductors of electricity indicates that bonding in these compounds does not give rise to any ions (covalent bonds/sharing of electrons do not form charged particles).
samples.explanation:
• Low melting and boiling points show that carbon compounds are held together by weak intermolecular forces of attraction, unlike ionic compounds.
• Being poor conductors shows their covalent bonding does not produce free ions or charged particles needed to carry current.

samples.text: Why is the conversion of ethanol to ethanoic acid an oxidation reaction ? Name the oxidising agent used in this conversion. Write chemical equation for this oxidation reaction. How is this reaction different from the reaction in which ethanol burns in the presence of oxygen ?
samples.answer:
• Oxygen is added to ethanol to produce ethanoic acid, which is why it is an oxidation reaction.
• Oxidising agent: Alkaline potassium permanganate (or Acidified potassium dichromate).
• Equation: CH3CH2OH —[Alkaline KMnO4 + Heat, or acidified K2Cr2O7 + Heat]→ CH3COOH
• Difference: this is an oxidation reaction, whereas ethanol burning in oxygen is a combustion reaction.
samples.explanation:
• Oxidation adds oxygen to a substance — here, ethanol gains an oxygen atom to form ethanoic acid.
• Oxidising agent: alkaline KMnO4 or acidified K2Cr2O7, with heat.
• Equation: CH3CH2OH → CH3COOH using the oxidising agent and heat.
• Difference: this controlled oxidation differs from combustion, where ethanol burns directly in oxygen releasing heat and light, producing CO2 and H2O.

samples.text:
(a) Define the term "Functional group of a carbon compound". Write the formula of functional group present in (i) propanol and (ii) propanone.
(b) Name the process of conversion of (i) ethanol to ethene and (ii) ethanol to ethanoic acid. Write the reaction equation stating the conditions required for each of the reactions to occur.
samples.answer:
(a)
    • Functional group: The element (or group) replacing hydrogen in a carbon compound is called a heteroatom; these heteroatoms confer special properties to the compound and are known as functional groups.
    • (i) Functional group in propanol: –OH (Alcohol)
    • (ii) Functional group in propanone: >C=O (Ketone)
(b)
    • (i) Dehydration: C₂H₅OH →(443 K, Conc. H₂SO₄, excess) C₂H₄ + H₂O (ethanol → ethene)
    • (ii) Oxidation: C₂H₅OH →(Alkaline KMnO₄/heat) CH₃COOH (ethanol → ethanoic acid)
samples.explanation:
(a)
    • A functional group is a heteroatom or group of atoms replacing hydrogen in a carbon chain, giving the compound its characteristic chemical properties. Propanol contains the –OH (alcohol) group; propanone contains the >C=O (ketone) group.
(b)
    • (i) Ethanol converts to ethene by dehydration: heating with excess concentrated sulphuric acid at 443 K removes water, C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O.
    • (ii) Ethanol converts to ethanoic acid by oxidation: heating with alkaline potassium permanganate oxidises the alcohol group to a carboxylic acid, C₂H₅OH → CH₃COOH.

samples.text: Electrolysis of water is a decomposition reaction. The mass ratio (MH : MO) of hydrogen and oxygen gases liberated at the electrodes during electrolysis of water is :

samples.text: What is a chemical reaction ? Describe one activity each to show that a chemical change has occurred in which (i) change of colour, and (ii) change in temperature has taken place.
samples.answer:
• A chemical reaction involves the breaking and making of bonds between atoms to produce new substances (reactants change into products).
(i)
    • Colour change: add lead nitrate solution to potassium iodide solution in a test tube — the colourless solution changes to a yellow precipitate.
    • Pb(NO3)2 + 2KI → PbI2↓ (yellow) + 2KNO3 (or any other example)
(ii)
    • Temperature change: calcium oxide reacts vigorously with water to produce slaked lime (calcium hydroxide), releasing a large amount of heat.
    • CaO(s) + H2O(l) → Ca(OH)2(aq) + Heat (or any other example)
samples.explanation:
• A chemical reaction is a process in which bonds between atoms break and new bonds form, converting reactants into new products, often with a visible sign such as colour or temperature change.
(i)
    • Colour change: lead nitrate solution mixed with potassium iodide solution turns from colourless to a yellow precipitate.
    • Pb(NO3)2 + 2KI → PbI2↓ (yellow) + 2KNO3.
(ii)
    • Temperature change: calcium oxide reacting with water is a highly exothermic activity.
    • CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2 + Heat, releasing a large amount of heat and forming slaked lime as the product.

samples.text: Heat produced per second due to a current in a resistor of 4 Ω is 400 joules. Calculate the potential difference across the resistor.
samples.answer:
Given: H = 400 J, R = 4Ω, t = 1 s
H = V²/R × t
400 = V²/4 × 1
V² = 1600
∴ V = 40 V
samples.explanation:
• H = (V²/R) × t, using the given values 400 = V²/4 × 1
• Rearranging, V² = 400 × 4 = 1600
• V = √1600 = 40 V, the potential difference developed across the resistor.

samples.text:
(a) Define one ampere.
(b) The resistance of a wire of 0.01 cm radius is 14 Ω. If the resistivity of the material of the wire is 44 × 10⁻⁸ Ωm, find the length of the wire. (Given π = 22/7)
samples.answer:
(a)
    • When 1 coulomb of charge flows through any cross-section of a conductor in 1 second, the electric current flowing through it is 1 ampere.
    • 1A = 1C/1s
(b)
    Given: r = 0.01 cm = 0.01×10⁻² m, ρ = 44×10⁻⁸ Ωm, R = 14Ω
    R = ρl/A
    l = RA/ρ = (14×22×(0.01×10⁻²)²)/(7×44×10⁻⁸)
    ∴ l = 1.0 m
samples.explanation:
(a)
    • One ampere is the current flowing when 1 coulomb of charge passes through a cross-section of a conductor in 1 second (1A = 1C/1s).
(b)
    Given: r = 0.01 cm = 0.01×10⁻² m, R = 14Ω, ρ = 44×10⁻⁸ Ωm
    A = πr²
    l = RA/ρ = (14 × 22 × (0.01×10⁻²)²)/(7 × 44×10⁻⁸)
    l = 1.0 m
    ∴ The length of the wire is 1.0 metre.

samples.text:
(i) Which type of circuits — series or parallel, should be used when you have to operate different electrical gadgets in your house ? List two reasons for your answer.
(ii) Find the current flowing through the following electric circuit :
(see image for circuit diagram)
samples.answer:
(i)
    • Parallel Circuit
    • Each electrical appliance has its own switch due to which it can be turned ON and OFF separately.
    • If one electrical appliance stops working, others remain unaffected.
    • Each appliance has equal potential difference and draws current as per its requirement.
    • The total resistance in parallel circuit decreases. (any two)
(ii)
    • Combined resistance of the series, R1 = 6Ω + 6Ω = 12Ω
    • Combined resistance of parallel grouping of 6Ω and R1 = 12Ω, resistors is R2, where 1/R2 = 1/6 + 1/12 = 3/12
    • R2 = 4.0Ω
    • Total resistance of circuit = R = 3 + 4 + 3 = 10Ω
    • Current flowing = I = V/R = 4.5 V/10Ω = 0.45 A
samples.explanation:
(i)
    • Parallel circuits should be used, since each appliance gets its own switch and can be turned on/off independently.
    • If one appliance fails, the others keep working, and each appliance still receives the full supply voltage.
(ii)
Given: 3Ω, 6Ω, 3Ω in the outer loop; two 6Ω resistors forming a parallel branch; battery = 4.5 V (see image for circuit diagram)
    • Series pair in the branch: 6Ω + 6Ω = 12Ω
    • This 12Ω combines in parallel with the other 6Ω: 1/R2 = 1/6 + 1/12, R2 = 4Ω
    • Total resistance: R = 3 + 4 + 3 = 10Ω
    • Current: I = V/R = 4.5/10 = 0.45 A

samples.text: Differentiate between self-pollination and cross pollination. Which one of the two is better for the survival of species ? Give reason to justify your answer.
samples.answer:
Self-Pollination:
    • Pollen grains are transferred from stamen to the stigma of the same flower.
Cross Pollination:
    • Transfer of pollen grains from stamen of one flower to the stigma of another flower of same species.
Better for survival:
    • Cross pollination is better as it leads to more variations which is better for survival of the species over time.
samples.explanation:
• Self-pollination transfers pollen within the same flower, producing offspring genetically similar to the parent.
• Cross-pollination transfers pollen between different flowers of the same species, mixing genetic material from two parents.
• Cross-pollination is better for species survival because it introduces greater genetic variation, improving the population's ability to adapt to changing environmental conditions and resist diseases.

samples.text: How is lymph formed ? State its important function.
samples.answer:
• Through the pores present in the walls of capillaries some amount of plasma, proteins and blood cells escape into intercellular spaces in the tissue to form the tissue fluid called lymph.
• Lymph carries digested and absorbed fat from intestine / drains excess fluid from extracellular space back into the blood.

samples.text:

(i) Saliva
(ii) Bile Juice
(iii) Pancreatic Juice
samples.answer:
(i) Salivary amylase - converts Starch to sugar
(ii) Bile salts – changing the acidic food alkaline/ emulsifies fats.
(iii) Trypsin – Helps in digestion of proteins / Lipase – Breaking down emulsified fats
samples.explanation:

• (ii) Bile juice contains bile salts, which neutralise the acidic food coming from the stomach and emulsify fats into smaller droplets for easier digestion.

samples.text:

(ii) Discuss the role of the pancreas and bile juice in the digestion of food in human beings.
(iii) How is the small intestine designed to absorb digested food ?
samples.answer:
(i)
    • Herbivores eating grass need a longer small intestine to digest cellulose.
    • Meat is easier to digest, so meat-eating animals (carnivores) have a shorter small intestine.
(ii)
    • Role of Pancreas: secretes pancreatic juice containing trypsin (for digesting proteins) and lipase (for breaking down emulsified fats).
    • Role of Bile: emulsifies fats and makes the medium alkaline in the small intestine so that pancreatic enzymes can act.
(iii)
    • The inner lining of the small intestine has numerous finger-like projections called villi, which increase the surface area for absorption of food.
    • The villi are richly supplied with blood vessels which carry the absorbed food to every cell of the body.
samples.explanation:
(i)
    • Herbivores need a longer small intestine to digest cellulose from grass, while carnivores, eating easily digestible meat, have a shorter small intestine.
(ii)
    • Pancreas: secretes pancreatic juice with trypsin (digests proteins) and lipase (breaks down emulsified fats).
    • Bile: emulsifies fats and makes the intestinal medium alkaline so pancreatic enzymes can act effectively.
(iii)
    • The small intestine's lining has finger-like villi that increase surface area and are richly supplied with blood vessels to absorb and transport digested food to body cells.

samples.text: An object is placed at a distance of 10 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Use mirror formula to determine the position of the image formed by this mirror.
samples.answer:
Given: u = -10 cm, f = -15 cm
1/f = 1/v + 1/u
1/(-15) = 1/v + 1/(-10)
1/v = 1/(-15) + 1/10
v = +30 cm
∴ Position of image is 30 cm from the mirror.
samples.explanation:
• u = -10 cm, f = -15 cm; using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u
• 1/(-15) = 1/v + 1/(-10) → 1/v = 1/10 - 1/15 = 1/30
• v = +30 cm, so the image forms 30 cm behind the mirror, on the virtual side.

samples.text: An object of size 5 cm is placed at a distance of 30 cm from the optical centre of a converging lens of focal length 20 cm. Use lens formula to determine the position and size of the image formed.
samples.answer:
Position:
1/v - 1/u = 1/f
1/v - 1/(-30) = 1/(+20)
1/v + 1/30 = 1/20 => v = +60 cm
position is 60 cm from the lens
Size: m = hi/ho = v/u
= 60/(-30) = -2
hi = -2 x 5 cm = -10 cm
size of image is 10 cm (Enlarged)
samples.explanation:
• Given: ho = 5 cm, u = -30 cm, f = +20 cm
• 1/v - 1/u = 1/f
• 1/v - 1/(-30) = 1/20
• 1/v = 1/20 - 1/30 = 1/60
• v = +60 cm
• ∴ Image at 60 cm, opposite side (real).
• m = v/u = 60/(-30) = -2
• hi = m x ho = -2 x 5 = -10 cm
• ∴ Image size = 10 cm; real, inverted, enlarged.

samples.text:

samples.answer:
(i)
    • The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.
    • The incident ray, the normal to the mirror at the point of incidence, and the reflected ray, all lie in the same plane.
(ii)
Given: u = −15 cm, f = −10 cm (concave mirror), h = 5.0 cm
    • Mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u
    • 1/v = −1/10 + 1/15
    • 1/v = −1/30
    • v = −30 cm — the screen must be placed at a distance of 30 cm from the mirror, in front of it.
    • Magnification: m = h′/h = −v/u
    • h′ = (−v/u) × h = −(−30/−15) × 5

samples.text: How and why is an electric fuse used in an electric circuit ? Briefly describe its function.
samples.answer:
• An electric fuse is placed in series with the device to prevent the electric circuit from possible damage by stopping the flow of unduly high electric current.
• If current larger than the specified value flows through the circuit, the fuse melts and breaks the electric circuit.

samples.text:

(b) If 10,000 J energy is available at the producer level, how much energy will be available to the secondary consumers ? Give reason to justify your answer.
samples.answer:
(a)
    • The energy captured by plants does not revert to solar input, and the energy that passes to herbivores does not revert back to autotrophs.
    • As energy moves progressively through the trophic levels, it is no longer available to the previous level.
    • The energy available at each trophic level gets progressively diminished due to loss of energy at each level. (any two)
(b)
    • 100 J
    • Autotrophs (10000 J) → Primary consumer (1000 J) → Secondary consumer (100 J)
    • Only 10% of the energy of the organic matter of the previous trophic level is transferred to the next trophic level (10% law).
samples.explanation:

    • Energy captured by producers never reverts back to the sun or to the previous trophic level once it moves forward through the food chain.
    • Energy available at each trophic level diminishes progressively, so it cannot flow backward.
(b)
    • Only 10% of energy transfers at each trophic level (10% law): 10,000 J → 1,000 J (primary consumers) → 100 J (secondary consumers).
    ∴ Secondary consumers receive 100 J.
